name: numpy

files.tests/test_grid.py:
import numpy as np

from app import grid


def test_cell_count():
    assert grid.cell_count((3, 4)) == 12


def test_to_grid():
    g = grid.to_grid(np.arange(6), 2)
    assert g.shape == (2, 3)
    assert g[1].tolist() == [3, 4, 5]


def test_stack_days():
    s = grid.stack_days([1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6])
    assert s.shape == (3, 2)


def test_totals_negative_axis():
    g = np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3)
    assert grid.totals(g, -1).tolist() == [3, 12]
    assert int(grid.totals(g, (0, 1))) == 15

notes: Old: numpy 1.26.4 on Python 3.11 (the last 1.x, the usual pin before NumPy 2). New: 2.5.5 on Python 3.12, the current release: in1d, row_stack, trapz, percentile(interpolation=) and reshape(newshape=) were deprecated in 2.0/2.1 and are gone by 2.5, so they break instead of warning (on 2.0-2.3 they would be DEPRECATED). np.NaN, np.float_ and np.row_stack are MOVED: each is the same object as its successor in 1.26.4. numpy.core.numeric is DEPRECATED: its DeprecationWarning comes from the module __getattr__ at import time, not from a call, so it is not in expected_warnings. Almost every numpy callable is a C object on both sides (ufuncs, _ArrayFunctionDispatcher), so this toy measures the compiled-API case (FINDINGS G1). The NEP 50 change is visible only at np.round, the numpy call that receives the promoted value: the float32 arithmetic itself runs through C number slots. Not covered: ndarray.itemset/newbyteorder, np.unique(return_inverse=) shapes, scalar reprs ('np.float64(1.5)'), uint8 overflow under NEP 50.
